code_exercises.title: Importance Sampling Unbiased/Self-Normalized Estimators & Kish ESS
code_exercises.prompt_markdown:
Implement `importance_sampling_estimator(f_vals, p_target_vals, q_proposal_vals)` for $N$ samples $x_i \sim q(x)$ with importance weights $w_i = p(x_i) / q(x_i)$. Return `(est_unbiased, est_self_norm, ess)`:
- `est_unbiased`: $\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N f(x_i) w_i$,
- `est_self_norm`: $\frac{\sum_{i=1}^N f(x_i) w_i}{\sum_{i=1}^N w_i}$,
- `ess`: Kish Effective Sample Size $\frac{(\sum_{i=1}^N w_i)^2}{\sum_{i=1}^N w_i^2} \in [1, N]$.

import math
import numpy as np

    where ess = (sum w_i)^2 / sum(w_i^2)."""

code_exercises.title: Von Neumann Rejection Sampler & Envelope Dominance Guard
code_exercises.signature: def von_neumann_rejection_filter(x_proposals, u_accept, p_vals, q_vals, c_bound):
code_exercises.prompt_markdown:
Implement `von_neumann_rejection_filter(x_proposals, u_accept, p_vals, q_vals, c_bound)`:
1. Validate `c_bound > 0`, `q_vals > 0`, `p_vals >= 0`, and the envelope condition $p_i \le c_{\text{bound}} q_i + 10^{-12}$ for all $i$; raise `ValueError` if violated!
2. Accept draws satisfying $u_i \cdot c_{\text{bound}} \cdot q_i < p_i$ and return `(accepted_x, acceptance_rate)`.
code_exercises.starter_code:
import math
import numpy as np

def von_neumann_rejection_filter(x_proposals, u_accept, p_vals, q_vals, c_bound):
    """Verify p_vals <= c_bound * q_vals + 1e-12 (raising ValueError on envelope violation)
    and accept draws where u_accept * c_bound * q_vals < p_vals."""
    raise NotImplementedError('Implement von_neumann_rejection_filter')

REJECTION_ENVELOPE_BOUND_C_OMISSION_GAP.diagnostic_rationale: Von Neumann rejection compares u_i < p(x_i) / [c_bound * q(x_i)]; omitting c_bound clips p/q > 1 and distorts the peak.

REJECTION_ENVELOPE_VIOLATION_GUARD_GAP.diagnostic_rationale: When c_bound * q(x_i) < p(x_i) anywhere, the envelope fails to cover p(x) and must raise ValueError rather than silently clipping the peak.

code_exercises.title: Cholesky Factorization & Multivariate Correlated Gaussian Sampler
code_exercises.prompt_markdown:
Implement `cholesky_correlated_gaussian_draw(mean_vec, cov_matrix, z_standard)`:
1. Factor the $D \times D$ symmetric positive-definite covariance matrix $\boldsymbol{\Sigma} = \mathbf{L}\mathbf{L}^T$ into its lower-triangular Cholesky factor `L_lower`.
2. Map standard normal draws `z_standard` of shape `(D, M)` to correlated draws $\mathbf{X} = \boldsymbol{\mu}_{:, \text{None}} + \mathbf{L}\mathbf{Z}$ of shape `(D, M)`.
Return `(L_lower, samples)`.
code_exercises.starter_code:
import math
import numpy as np

def cholesky_correlated_gaussian_draw(mean_vec, cov_matrix, z_standard):
    """Factor cov_matrix = L_lower @ L_lower.T and return (L_lower, samples)
    where samples = mean_vec[:, None] + L_lower @ z_standard has shape (D, M)."""
    raise NotImplementedError('Implement cholesky_correlated_gaussian_draw')

CHOLESKY_TRANSPOSE_L_T_Z_ORIENTATION_GAP.diagnostic_rationale: With Sigma = L @ L.T (L lower-triangular), correlated samples require L @ z so <L z (L z)^T> = L <z z^T> L^T = L @ L.T = Sigma; using L.T @ z gives L.T @ L != Sigma.

CHOLESKY_CONTRACT_OR_MEAN_BROADCAST_GAP.diagnostic_rationale: Ensure L_lower is strictly lower-triangular (zeros above diagonal) and broadcast mean_vec as mu[:, None] across all M columns.
